parties: Sachin Agarwal, Shikha Agarwal, Aanjanayae Agarwal, Anadyae Agarwal, Suprateek Printing Private Limited (acquirers) / Sampann Utpadan India Limited (target)
headline: Sachin Agarwal group files SEBI Reg 31(4) disclosure for substantial acquisition in Sampann Utpadan India Limited
sum: Sachin Agarwal, Shikha Agarwal, Aanjanayae Agarwal, Anadyae Agarwal and Suprateek Printing Private Limited have disclosed a substantial acquisition of shares in Sampann Utpadan India Limited under SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011. The disclosure triggers mandatory open offer or shareholding threshold breach reporting requirements under the takeover code.
implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosure signals either a crossing of 5% shareholding threshold (requiring disclosure within 4 trading days) or commencement of concert party/aggregation under the takeover regulations-practitioners should examine the disclosure form to verify the exact trigger, shareholding % and whether an open offer under Regulation 3(1) or Regulation 8 will follow.
detail: Sampann Utpadan India Limited is the listed target; the acquirers comprise individual family members (Sachin, Shikha, Aanjanayae, Anadyae Agarwal) and Suprateek Printing Private Limited, suggesting a family-led acquisition group or concert party structure. The Regulation 31(4) disclosure to NSE formalises the crossing of a substantial shareholding threshold and is the mandatory first step in the SEBI takeover notification process. No open offer amount, acquisition price, or final shareholding % is disclosed in the headline filing; these will appear in the detailed disclosure form (Form A or Form B) itself.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 3(1)
framework.note: Central-mandatory open offer triggered when acquirer(s) acquire 25% or more of voting capital or control of target; defines concert party aggregation.
Central-exemptions from open offer (e.g., exemptions for acquisitions by persons acting in concert if no single person acquires >5%).
Central-requires disclosure within 4 trading days of crossing 5% shareholding threshold; mandatory notification to exchange and company.
Central-conditions for open offer: price determination, minimum shares to be acquired, timing and settlement of offer.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, Section 15
framework.note: Foundational-grants SEBI power to make regulations regarding substantial acquisitions and takeovers; substantive jurisdiction.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013, Section 5 and Schedule XII (Concert Party definition)
framework.note: Supplementary-defines concert party and related-party aggregation for shareholding calculations under takeover law.

framework.ref: BSE/NSE Listing Rules, Clause 24 (Substantial acquisition disclosures)
framework.note: Exchange compliance-both BSE and NSE have adopted the SEBI takeover code; disclosure must be filed with both exchanges if listed on both.

conditions: Substantial acquisition crossing 5% shareholding threshold (exact % to be disclosed in full Form A/B)
Concert party structure among family members and Suprateek Printing Private Limited (if aggregated, will trigger higher open offer threshold)
Possible subsequent open offer at regulated floor price under Regulation 8, if 25%+ threshold crossed
approvals: Possible SEBI/CCI pre-approval for control change (if applicable under M&A codes)
Target company board acknowledgment and shareholder disclosures
structure.novel: Family-led acquisition through mix of individual family members and private company vehicle (Suprateek Printing); may test concert party aggregation rules if shareholding % and degree of control are material.

triggers.note: Mandatory disclosure within 4 trading days of crossing 5% shareholding threshold in a listed company.
If aggregated shareholding reaches 25%, mandatory open offer at regulated floor price is triggered.
Individual family members acting together with corporate vehicle may be deemed concert party under takeover code, requiring shareholding aggregation.
